<div class="hero-brand">
  <img src="images/cornell_seal.svg" alt="Cornell University" class="cornell-seal">

<div class="hero-summary">
  <p>Every empirical project begins with data somebody had to find, fetch,
  clean, check, and shape — work your methods courses assume is already done.
  This course teaches it, across the raw material economists now use: messy
  tables, text, documents, images, audio, and maps. AI tools are part of the
  toolkit from early on — and precisely because a model can draft competent
  code in seconds, the skill this course grades is <em>verification</em>:
  knowing whether the result is right. Homework is a single running
  investigation of the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, taken through a
  new data family each week; there are no prerequisites.</p>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  // The "we are here" line: mark the next class day, but only while the
  // Fall 2026 term is running — in any other year this page is an archive
  // and the script does nothing.
  var now = new Date();
  if (now < new Date(2026, 7, 20) || now > new Date(2026, 11, 10)) return;
  var months = {Jan: 0, Feb: 1, Mar: 2, Apr: 3, May: 4, Jun: 5,
                Jul: 6, Aug: 7, Sep: 8, Oct: 9, Nov: 10, Dec: 11};
  var today = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate());
  var rows = document.querySelectorAll('.grouped-schedule tbody tr');
  for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
    if (rows[i].classList.contains('part-row')) continue;
    var cells = rows[i].cells;
    for (var j = 0; j < cells.length; j++) {
      var m = cells[j].textContent.trim()
        .match(/^(?:Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) ([A-Z][a-z]{2}) (\d{1,2})$/);
      if (!m) continue;
      if (new Date(2026, months[m[1]], +m[2]) >= today) {
        rows[i].classList.add('today-line');
        cells[j].classList.add('today-cell');
        return;
      }
      break;
    }
  }
})();
</script>
